items.text: Ted W. Lieu is the U.S. Representative for California's 36th Congressional District and is serving his sixth term. He sits on the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees and serves as Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus. He previously served in the California State Assembly and State Senate, and on the Torrance City Council. Lieu is a lawyer and a former active-duty Air Force officer who retired from the U.S. Air Force Reserve with the rank of colonel.

He sits on the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees and serves as Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus.
He previously served in the California State Assembly and State Senate, and on the Torrance City Council.
Lieu is a lawyer and a former active-duty Air Force officer who retired from the U.S. Air Force Reserve with the rank of colonel.

items.text: In 2026, Lieu co-introduced the AI Kill Switch Act, which would require developers of advanced AI systems to maintain the ability to shut down their systems. He says he co-authored a provision in the 2025 National Defense Authorization Act to keep human control over nuclear launch decisions. He opposed a bill he said would cut health insurance for over 2.3 million Californians and introduced a bill to guarantee congressional office access for people in immigration detention. He has pushed for a national film and television tax credit. He served as an impeachment manager for the second impeachment trial of President Donald Trump.

items.text: In Congress, Lieu passed laws to secure $35 million for seismic retrofits at the West Los Angeles VA and reauthorize a homeless veterans advisory committee. In 2026, he announced securing $13.7 million in federal funding for 14 local projects, including $1.09 million for a Beverly Hills water reliability project and $850,000 for a supportive housing project. His fentanyl overdose prevention bill, Tyler's Law, passed the House in September 2026. In the California legislature, he authored a ban on gay conversion therapy for minors and co-authored the state's Global Warming Solutions Act.
